subject.title: chore: add fail-closed publication security preflight

question: Should OpenClaw require a per-worktree publication manifest for normal contributor pushes when a local Git hook cannot enforce that requirement against bypasses or altered local configuration?
rationale: This is a repository policy and security-boundary choice, not a mechanical defect that can be resolved safely without deciding whether local checks are advisory or whether remote enforcement is required.

options.title: Keep it advisory
options.body: Retain a narrow optional preflight command and describe it as local contributor guidance rather than a fail-closed security control.

options.title: Enforce remotely
options.body: Design a GitHub-side branch-protection or required-check mechanism that can actually reject publication without relying on contributor-local hooks.

options.title: Decline the workflow
options.body: Do not add a new mandatory publication-manifest process if its operational cost is not justified by a remotely enforceable threat model.

recommendation.title: Keep it advisory
recommendation.body: Retain a narrow optional preflight command and describe it as local contributor guidance rather than a fail-closed security control.

likelyOwner.reason: They need to own the repository-wide contributor workflow and decide whether the claimed security boundary belongs in remote controls.
